titleEn: The Song of the Cid — The Infantes ask to take their wives to Carrión; Ximena's farewell (tiradas 124–125, lines 2543–2617)
part: Tiradas 124–125 · The Infantes ask to take their wives to Carrión; Ximena's farewell (lines 2543–2617)

sentences.t:
—“Pidamos nuestras mugieres al Çid Campeador,
digamos que las llevaremos a tierras de Carrión,
enseñar las hemos do [e]llas heredad[a]s son.
sentences.i: “Let us ask the Çid Campeador for our wives; let us say we will take them to the lands of Carrión and show them where their estates lie.
sentences.n: Tirada 124 (assonance ó) — the Infantes resolve to shame the Çid's daughters; they ask the Çid for their wives, to take them to Carrión; the Çid consents, and the trousseau he gives his daughters; the Infantes make ready to go; the daughters take leave of their father (Pidal: Los infantes deciden afrentar a las hijas del Cid. — Piden al Cid sus mujeres para llevarlas a Carrión. — El Cid accede. Ajuar que da a sus hijas. — Los infantes dispónense a marchar. — Las hijas despídense del padre). The line-ends run Campeador, Carrión, son, sabor, león, valor …: stressed ó, now and then with an e after it (omnes, enperadores, bendiçiones). The Infantes' plotting speech, begun at v. 2540 at the end of the last part, runs on across the tirada break: Pidal opens the new tirada with a fresh dash and quotation mark (—“), and opens one again at v. 2552, where, on Lidforss's view (Pidal's note to v. 2553), the other brother takes up the words. Pidamos, digamos, present subjunctive, 'let us ask, let us say'. mugieres = mujeres, 'wives'. enseñar las hemos, the split future: the infinitive, then the pronoun, then hemos, 'we will show them' (= las enseñaremos); the pattern returns at vv. 2546, 2563, 2564-5, 2568. do = donde, 'where'. [e]llas heredad[a]s son, 'they are endowed (with lands)', heredar 'to give a heritage to': the e of ellas and the a of heredadas are Pidal's italics (whether his italic also takes in the final s is not certain; it is read as roman). The lands meant are the arras the Infantes settled on their brides (vv. 2564-5, 2570).

sentences.i: We will take them out of Valencia, out of the Campeador's keeping; then on the road we will do as we please with them, before they can throw in our faces what happened with the lion.
sentences.n: Sacar las hemos, split future again, 'we will take them out'. de poder del Campeador, 'out of the Campeador's power', from under his protection. en la carrera, 'on the road'. feremos = haremos, future of fer (fazer), f- for modern h-; feremos nuestro sabor, 'we will do our pleasure', a so sabor being 'at one's will'. The threat is left unspoken here; the rubric names it: afrentar, 'to shame, outrage'. ante que = antes que, 'before'; retrayan, present subjunctive of retraer, 'to reproach, cast up'. Pidal's note to v. 2548: 'antes que nos echen en cara lo que sucedió con el león' — 'before they throw in our faces what happened with the lion'. cuntió = aconteció, 'befell' (cuntir); del león, 'concerning the lion': the Çid's lion that broke loose in tirada 112, when the Infantes hid in terror.

sentences.i: We are by birth of the line of the Counts of Carrión! We will carry off great riches, worth a great price; we will dishonour the Campeador's daughters.”
sentences.n: The line closes with ! and no ¡, as printed. Nos, 'we', stressed: the subject pronoun, not the Nos (= non + se) of vv. 2569 and 2617. de natura, 'by birth, by lineage'; somos de co[m]des, 'we are of counts', of comital stock — the m of comdes is Pidal's. Their father is Count Don Gonzalo. Averes … grandes, the adjective set apart from its noun across the caesura; levaremos = llevaremos, 'we will carry off'; valen grant valor, 'are worth great worth', the poem's doubling for emphasis. escarniremos, future of escarnir, 'to mock, shame, dishonour' (whence escarnio, 'mockery', v. 2464): the word for what will be done to the daughters. Canpeador, with n before p, as printed. The first speaker's words close here.

sentences.t:
—“D' aquestos averes sienpre seremos ricos omnes,
podremos casar con fijas de reyes o de enperadores
ca de natura somos de co[m]des de Carrión.
sentences.l:
—“From these goods always we-will-be rich men,
we-will-be-able to-marry with daughters of kings or of emperors
for by birth we-are of counts of Carrión.
sentences.i: —“With this wealth we shall always be great lords; we shall be able to marry the daughters of kings or of emperors, for by birth we are of the line of the Counts of Carrión.
sentences.n: A new speaker, opening with —“ as Pidal prints it. Pidal's note to v. 2553: 'Para el orgullo de los infantes, v. p. 91-92. Observa acertadamente Lidforss que estos versos deben considerarse repartidos entre los dos hermanos; uno remeda neciamente las palabras del otro, produciendo cierto efecto cómico que, bien manejado por un juglar festivo, causaría gran risa en el auditorio' — 'On the Infantes' pride, see pp. 91–92 [of his introduction]. Lidforss rightly observes that these lines should be taken as shared between the two brothers; one foolishly apes the other's words, producing a certain comic effect which, well handled by a merry minstrel, would set the audience laughing.' Hence the echoes: v. 2554 repeats v. 2549, and vv. 2555–2556 repeat vv. 2551 and 2548. D' aquestos averes, 'from these goods'. sienpre, with n, as printed. ricos omnes, 'rich men', the ricos hombres, the highest rank of the nobility below the counts. casar con, 'to marry'. v. 2553 ends without punctuation, as printed. ca, 'for'.

sentences.t:
Assí las escarniremos a fijas del Campeador,
antes que nos retrayan lo que f[o] del león.”
sentences.l:
Thus them we-will-shame the daughters of-the Campeador,
before that us they-cast-up what wa[s] of-the lion.”
sentences.i: So we will shame the Campeador's daughters, before they throw in our faces what happened with the lion.”
sentences.n: Assí las escarniremos a fijas del Campeador, the object said twice: las, 'them', and then, with the personal a, fijas del Campeador, which has no article. antes que, the full form of the ante que of v. 2548. f[o] = fue, 'was', here 'happened', the o Pidal's. The second brother echoes the first almost word for word (see the note to v. 2552). Here the speech that began at v. 2540 closes.

sentences.t:
Con aqueste conssejo amos tornados son,
fabló Ferran[t] Gonçál[v]ez e fizo callar la cort:
sentences.l:
With this counsel both returned are,
spoke Ferran[t] Gonçál[v]ez and made be-silent the court:
sentences.i: With this plan the two of them went back, and Fernando González spoke and silenced the court:
sentences.n: conssejo, 'counsel, plan', what they 'took counsel' over at v. 2537. tornados son, 'they are returned', the perfect of a verb of motion made with ser, as often in Old Spanish (cf. modern French ils sont retournés). Ferran[t] Gonçál[v]ez, 'Fernando González' (house rendering), the t and the v Pidal's. fizo callar la cort, 'made the court fall silent'; cort, 'court', without its final e.

sentences.t:
“Sí vos vala el Criador, Çid Campeador!
que plega a doña Ximena e primero a vos
e a Minaya Álbar Fáñez e a quantos aquí son:
dadnos nuestras mugieres que avemos a bendiçiones;
sentences.l:
“So you may-help the Creator, Çid Campeador!
that it-may-please Doña Ximena and first you
and Minaya Álbar Fáñez and as-many-as here are:
give-us our wives that we-have by blessings;
sentences.i: “So may the Creator help you, Çid Campeador! May it please Doña Ximena — and you first of all — and Minaya Álvar Fáñez and everyone here: give us our wives, whom we have wed with the Church's blessing.
sentences.n: Sí vos vala el Criador, 'so may the Creator help you' (house rendering): sí, 'so', with the present subjunctive vala of valer, 'to avail, help'. The line closes with ! and no ¡, as printed. que plega …, 'that it may please', plega present subjunctive of plazer (= plazca); the courteous preamble before a request. primero a vos, 'and first (to) you'. Minaya Álbar Fáñez, 'Minaya Álvar Fáñez' in the English (house rendering). quantos aquí son, 'as many as are here', son where modern Spanish says están. dadnos, imperative + nos, 'give us'. que avemos a bendiçiones, 'whom we have by blessings', married with the Church's blessing (the bendiciones given at the weddings of tirada 109–111): their claim is lawful.

sentences.t:
levar las hemos a nuestras tierras de Carrión,
meter las hemos en arras que les diemos por onores;
veran vuestras fijas lo que avemos nos,
los fijos que oviéremos en qué avrán partiçión.”
sentences.l:
take them we-will to our lands of Carrión,
put them we-will in arras that to-them we-gave as estates;
will-see your daughters what we-have we,
the sons that we-may-have in which they-will-have share.”
sentences.i: We will take them to our lands of Carrión and put them in possession of the lands we gave them as their marriage settlement; your daughters will see what we own, the lands in which the sons we may have will have their share.”
sentences.n: Three split futures: levar las hemos, 'we will take them'; meter las hemos, 'we will put them'. Line 2564-5 is one line that bears two numbers in Pidal's print; the count runs on at 2566. Pidal's note to v. 2564-5: 'meter en arras, "posesionar de las arras"; onores, "heredades", v. 289. Las arras son las villas y tierras que el varón da a la mujer al casarse con ella. La mujer no podía disponer libremente de las arras cuando tenía hijos del donante, pues tenía que reservarlas para dejarlas en herencia a esos hijos; así se explica el verso 2567, "verán las heredades en que tendrán parte nuestros hijos"' — 'meter en arras, "to put in possession of the arras"; onores, "estates", v. 289. The arras are the towns and lands the husband gives the wife on marrying her. The wife could not freely dispose of the arras once she had children by the giver, for she had to keep them to leave as inheritance to those children; this explains v. 2567: "they will see the estates in which our sons will have a share".' diemos = dimos, 'we gave'; por onores, 'as estates' (onor, the house 'estate'). veran, unaccented as printed (= verán), 'will see'; lo que avemos nos, 'what we have', aver 'to have, own' as a full verb, with the subject pronoun nos at the end. oviéremos, future subjunctive of aver, '(whom) we may have'; en qué, accented as printed, 'in which'; avrán partiçión, 'will have a share'. The speech closes here.

sentences.t:
Nos curiava de [fonta] [mio] Çid el Campeador:
“Darvos he mis fijas e algo de lo mio;
sentences.l:
Not-himself was-wary of [outrage] [my] Çid the Campeador:
“Give-you I-will my daughters and something of the mine;
sentences.i: My Çid the Campeador had no suspicion of the outrage: “I will give you my daughters, and something of what is mine.
sentences.n: Order: Pidal prints v. 2569 before v. 2568, keeping both numbers; his print order and numbers are followed here. Nos = non + se, 'not … himself' (not the Nos 'we' of v. 2549). Pidal's note to v. 2569: 'El verbo curiar, comp. 329, se usa aquí reflexivo: "no se recelaba de que le preparasen una afrenta"' — 'The verb curiar (compare v. 329) is used here reflexively: "he had no suspicion that they were preparing an outrage for him".' curiava, imperfect of curiar, 'to guard, beware'. [fonta] and [mio] are both wholly Pidal's (two italic words either side of the caesura; whether they are one restoration or two is not certain): fonta, 'outrage, affront' (= afrenta). Darvos he, split future, 'I will give you' (= os daré). algo de lo mio, 'something of what is mine', the dowry he goes on to list; mio unaccented, as printed.

sentences.t:
vos les diestes villas por arras en tierras de Carrión,
yo quiéroles dar axuvar tres mill marcos de [valor];
sentences.l:
you to-them gave towns as arras in lands of Carrión,
I wish-to-them give trousseau three thousand marks of [value];
sentences.i: You gave them towns as their marriage portion in the lands of Carrión; I wish to give them a trousseau worth three thousand marks;
sentences.n: diestes = disteis, 'you gave'. villas por arras, 'towns as arras', the husband's marriage gift (see the note to v. 2564-5). quiéroles = les quiero, the pronoun after the verb at the head of the clause (after the subject yo), 'I wish to … them'. Pidal's note to v. 2571: 'axuvar, "ajuar", bienes que los padres de la novia dan a ésta con ocasión del matrimonio' — 'axuvar, "trousseau": goods that the bride's parents give her on the occasion of her marriage'. The Çid answers arras with axuvar: their gift with his. marcos, 'marks', a weight of silver. de [valor], 'in value', the whole word Pidal's.

sentences.i: I will give you mules and palfreys, sturdy and in prime condition, warhorses to be led at the right hand, strong and swift, and many garments of fine cloth and of silk brocade;
sentences.n: darvos e: most likely e = he, 'I will', written without h — the split future darvos he, as in v. 2575; read as 'and' ('both mules and palfreys') the line also stands, and the form is not certain. palafrés, 'palfreys', horses for ordinary riding. muy gruessos de sazón, 'very stout, in prime condition' (de sazón, 'in good condition'); the line ends without punctuation, as printed, and runs on to the warhorses. cavallos pora en diestro, 'horses for leading at the right hand': warhorses, led unmounted beside the rider until the fight (cf. Old French destrier); pora = para. corredores, 'swift-running'. paños, 'cloths', woollen stuffs; çiclatones, costly silks.

sentences.t:
darvos he dos espadas, a Colada e a Tizón,
bien lo sabedes vos que las gané a guisa de varón;
sentences.l:
give-you I-will two swords, Colada and Tizón,
well it you-know you that them I-won in manner of man;
sentences.i: I will give you two swords, Colada and Tizón — you know well that I won them like a man;
sentences.n: darvos he, split future. a Colada e a Tizón, the personal a before the swords' names: the swords are named like persons. Colada the Çid won from the Count of Barcelona; Tizón from King Búcar (tiradas 118–119); Tizón 'Tizón' (house rendering). bien lo sabedes vos, the lo announcing the que-clause. a guisa de varón, 'in the manner of a man', manfully: the Çid's swords are his honour, and he gives them to the men who fled the lion.

sentences.t:
mios fijos sodes amos, quando mis fijas vos do;
allá me levades las telas del coraçón.
sentences.l:
my sons you-are both, since my daughters to-you I-give;
thither from-me you-take the tissues of-the heart.
sentences.i: you are both my sons, since I give you my daughters; you carry off with you the very strings of my heart.
sentences.n: mios fijos, 'my sons'. quando here causal, 'since, now that'. do = doy, 'I give'. allá, 'there, away there' (to Carrión). me, 'from me', the dative of the one who loses. las telas del coraçón, 'the membranes of the heart', the tissues that hold it: what is dearest. levades = lleváis.

sentences.t:
Que lo sepan en Gallizia e en Castiella e en León,
con que riqueza enbio mios yernos amos a dos.
sentences.l:
That it they-know in Galicia and in Castile and in León,
with what wealth I-send my sons-in-law both two.
sentences.i: Let them know it in Galicia, in Castile and in León, with what riches I send off both my sons-in-law.
sentences.n: Que lo sepan, que + present subjunctive, 'let them know it'. Gallizia, Castiella, León, the kingdoms of Alfonso's realm. con que riqueza, que unaccented as printed (= qué), 'with what wealth'. enbio, unaccented as printed (= envío), 'I send', present. amos a dos, 'both (of the) two'. The Çid's wealth is a public matter of honour.

sentences.t:
A mis fijas sirvades, que vuestras mugieres son;
si bien las servides, yo vos rendré buen galardón.”
sentences.l:
To my daughters you-should-serve, for your wives they-are;
if well them you-serve, I to-you will-render good reward.”
sentences.i: Serve my daughters well, for they are your wives; if you serve them well, I will give you a good reward.”
sentences.n: sirvades, present subjunctive, a softened command, 'serve'; servides, present indicative, 'you serve'. que, 'for'. Pidal's note to v. 2582: 'vos rendré, "os daré en pago"' — 'I will give you in return'. rendré, future of render, 'to render, repay'. galardón, 'reward'. The Çid's speech closes here.

sentences.i: The Infantes of Carrión agreed to this. Here they receive the Campeador's daughters, and begin to receive the gifts the Çid bestowed.
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 2583: 'Atorgado lo han esto, "asintieron a esto"' — 'they consented to this'. atorgar = otorgar, 'to grant, agree'; the object is doubled, lo and esto; iffantes, ff and no article, as printed. reçiben, 'receive', the Infantes; fijas del Campeador without an article, as often. conpieçan = comienzan, 'begin'. Pidal's note to v. 2585: 'mandó, "ofreció en don"' — 'offered as a gift': mandar here 'to bestow, assign', not 'command'.

sentences.t:
Quando son pagados a todo so sabor,
ya mandavan cargar iffantes de Carrión.
sentences.l:
When they-are satisfied to all their pleasure,
now they-were-ordering to-load Infantes of Carrión.
sentences.i: When they were satisfied entirely to their liking, the Infantes of Carrión gave orders for the loading.
sentences.n: pagados, 'satisfied' (pagar, 'to please, content'). a todo so sabor, 'wholly to their liking'; so = su. mandavan cargar, 'they ordered (the beasts) to be loaded', the baggage for the journey. Epic tense-mixing: son (present), mandavan (imperfect).

sentences.t:
Grandes son las nuevas por Valençia la mayor,
todos prenden armas e cavalgan a vigor,
por que escurren fijas del [Cid] a tierras de Carrión.
sentences.l:
Great are the news through Valençia the great,
all take arms and ride with vigour,
because they-escort daughters of-the [Cid] to lands of Carrión.
sentences.i: There is a great stir throughout Valencia the great: everyone takes up arms and mounts in haste, for they are seeing the Çid's daughters off to the lands of Carrión.
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 2588: 'Grandes son las nuevas, "gran actividad o animación hay"' — 'there is great activity, great bustle': nuevas here not 'news' but the stir of things happening. Valençia la mayor, 'Valencia the great'. prenden, 'take'. Pidal's note to v. 2589: 'a vigor, "con presteza", v. 1671' — 'with speed'. por que, 'because'. Pidal's note to v. 2590: 'escurren, "despiden", v. 1067' — escurrir, 'to see off, escort on the way'. [Cid], the whole word Pidal's, printed in italic and without the cedilla.

sentences.t:
Ya quieren cavalgar, en espidimiento son.
Amas hermanas, don Elvira e doña Sol,
fincaron los inojos antel Çid Campeador:
sentences.l:
Now they-wish to-ride, in leave-taking they-are.
Both sisters, Don Elvira and Doña Sol,
knelt the knees before-the Çid Campeador:
sentences.i: Now they are about to ride; the leave-taking has come. Both sisters, Doña Elvira and Doña Sol, knelt before the Çid Campeador:
sentences.n: quieren cavalgar, 'they want to ride', here 'they are about to ride'. en espidimiento son, 'they are in (the act of) leave-taking'; espidimiento = despedida. Amas = ambas, 'both'. don Elvira, so printed, with don before a woman's name; 'Doña Elvira' in the English, as elsewhere. fincaron los inojos, 'they knelt' (fincar 'to set, plant', inojos 'knees'), with initial f- for modern h- (hincar, hinojos). antel = ante el, 'before the'.

sentences.i: “We ask a grace of you, father, so may the Creator help you! You begot us, our mother bore us; here before us you are, the two of you, our lady and our lord.
sentences.n: Merçed vos pedimos, 'we ask a grace, a favour of you'. sí vos vala el Criador, the house 'so may the Creator help you'; the line closes with ! and no ¡, as printed. engendrastes = engendrasteis, 'you begot'. parió, 'bore' (parir). delant = delante, 'in front, before (us)': Ximena stands with the Çid. señora e señor, 'lady and lord': the daughters address their parents with the forms used to a liege lord.

sentences.t:
Agora nos enviades a tierras de Carrión,
debdo nos es a cunplir lo que mandáredes vos.
sentences.l:
Now us you-send to lands of Carrión,
duty to-us it-is to fulfil what may-command you.
sentences.i: Now you are sending us to the lands of Carrión; it is our duty to do whatever you command.
sentences.n: Agora = ahora, 'now'. enviades = enviáis. debdo = deuda, 'debt, obligation': debdo nos es, 'it is (a) duty to us'. a cunplir, 'to fulfil', with a before the infinitive. mandáredes, future subjunctive, 'whatever you shall command', with the subject vos after it.

sentences.t:
Assí vos pedimos merçed nos amas a dos,
que ayades vuestros menssajes en tierras de Carrión.”
sentences.l:
Thus from-you we-ask grace we both two,
that you-have your messages in lands of Carrión.”
sentences.i: So we both ask this grace of you: that you send us word in the lands of Carrión.”
sentences.n: nos amas a dos, 'we, both of the two', the subject set at the end. que ayades vuestros menssajes, 'that you have your messages (sent)', present subjunctive of aver: that letters and messengers from home may reach them. menssaje is both message and messenger. The daughters' speech closes here.

sentences.t: Abraçólas mio Çid e saludólas amas a dos.
sentences.l: Embraced-them my Çid and greeted-them both two.
sentences.i: My Çid embraced them, and kissed them both.
sentences.n: Abraçólas, saludólas, preterite + enclitic las, 'embraced them', 'greeted them'. Pidal's note to v. 2601: '"Las abrazó y las besó en la boca"; comp. 3030' — '"embraced them and kissed them on the mouth"; compare v. 3030': saludar here is the kiss of greeting and farewell. The tirada ends.

sentences.i: He did this, and the mother did it twice over: “Go, my daughters; from now on may the Creator keep you! You have our full favour, from me and from your father.
sentences.n: Tirada 125 (assonance á-a) — Ximena takes leave of her daughters; the Çid rides out to see the travellers off; evil omens (Pidal: Jimena despide a sus hijas. — El Cid cabalga para despedir a los viajeros. — Agüeros malos). The line-ends run doblava, vala, graçia, heredadas, casadas, besavan …: stressed á, then a. El[l]e = él, 'he', the full form of the pronoun with an added -e, the second l Pidal's. aquesto = esto, 'this'. lo doblava, 'was doubling it', did as much again: embraced and kissed them twice over. Andad, imperative, 'go'. d' aquí, 'from here, henceforth'. el Criador vos vala, 'may the Creator help you', vala present subjunctive; the line closes with ! and no ¡, as printed. bien avedes nuestra graçia, 'you surely have our favour': graçia, a parent's (or lord's) favour and blessing.

sentences.t:
Id a Carrión do sodes heredadas,
assí commo yo tengo, bien vos he casadas.”
sentences.l:
Go to Carrión where you-are endowed,
so as I hold, well you I-have married.”
sentences.i: Go to Carrión, where your estates are; as I see it, I have married you well.”
sentences.n: Id, imperative of ir, 'go'. do = donde. heredadas, 'endowed with lands' (cf. v. 2545). assí commo yo tengo, 'as I hold', tener 'to consider, believe'. bien vos he casadas, 'I have you well married', the participle casadas agreeing with the object vos (the daughters), as aver + participle still could. The mother speaks of the match as her own act; the hearers know the Infantes' plan of v. 2546. Ximena's words close here.

sentences.t:
Al padre e a la madre las manos les besavan;
amos las bendixieron e diéronles su graçia.
sentences.l:
To-the father and to the mother the hands to-them they-were-kissing;
both them blessed and gave-them their favour.
sentences.i: They kissed their father's and their mother's hands; both of them blessed them and gave them their favour.
sentences.n: Al padre e a la madre … les, the indirect object said twice, first with a, then with les. las manos … besavan, 'they kissed the hands', the act of homage and of filial leave-taking. amos, 'both' (the parents). bendixieron, preterite of bendezir, 'blessed'. diéronles = les dieron. su graçia, 'their favour' (cf. v. 2604).

sentences.t:
Mio Çid e los otros de cavalgar penssavan,
a grandes guarnimientos, a cavallos e armas.
sentences.l:
My Çid and the others of riding were-thinking,
with great attire, with horses and arms.
sentences.i: My Çid and the others made ready to ride, in splendid attire, with horses and arms.
sentences.n: penssar de + infinitive, 'to set about, make ready to'. Pidal's note to v. 2610: '"con magníficos vestidos, con caballos y armas"; comp. 1427' — '"in magnificent clothes, with horses and arms"; compare v. 1427'. guarnimientos, 'attire, finery'. The rubric: the Çid rides out to see the travellers off.

sentences.t:
Ya salien los ifantes de Valençia la clara,
espi[di]éndos de las dueñas e de todas su[e]s compañas.
sentences.l:
Now were-going-out the Infantes from Valençia the bright,
taking-leave-themselves of the ladies and of all thei[r] companies.
sentences.i: Now the Infantes were leaving Valencia the fair, taking their leave of the ladies and of all their companions.
sentences.n: salien = salían, 'were going out'. ifantes, with one f here, as printed. Valençia la clara, 'Valencia the bright, the fair'. espi[di]éndos = espidiéndose (despidiéndose), the gerund with se cut to s; the di is Pidal's (how far his italic runs here is not certain; the é is read as roman). dueñas, 'ladies' of the household. su[e]s = sus, 'their', the e Pidal's; compañas, 'companies, people', here the Çid's household whom they leave behind.

sentences.t:
Por la huerta de Valencia teniendo salien armas;
alegre va mio Çid con todas su[e]s compañas.
sentences.l:
Through the huerta of Valencia holding were-going-out arms;
glad goes my Çid with all hi[s] companies.
sentences.i: Out across the garden-plain of Valencia they rode, playing at arms; my Çid goes gladly with all his men.
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 2613: '"salían jugando las armas", v. 1577' — 'they went out playing at arms': teniendo … armas, 'handling arms', the mock combat and display of horsemanship that honoured a departure (cf. v. 1577). huerta, the irrigated garden-plain about the city; Valencia here without the cedilla, as printed. alegre va, 'glad he goes', the adjective for an adverb. su[e]s = sus, 'his', the e Pidal's.

sentences.t:
Víolo en los avueros el que en buen[a] cinxo espada,
que estos casamientos non serién sin alguna tacha.
Nos puede repentir, que casadas las ha amas.
sentences.l:
Saw-it in the omens he who in good[a] girded sword,
that these marriages not would-be without some stain.
Not-himself can repent, for married them he-has both.
sentences.i: He who in a good hour girded on his sword saw in the omens that these marriages would not be without some stain. But he cannot go back on it, for he has married them both.
sentences.n: Víolo = lo vio, 'he saw it', accented as printed. Pidal's note to v. 2615: 'avueros, "agüeros". Sobre el Cid agorero, v. p. 18' — 'omens; on the Çid as a reader of omens, see p. 18 [of his introduction]'. The Çid reads the flight of birds (cf. the crow at the start of the poem, v. 11). el que en buen[a] cinxo espada, the en buen ora formula with ora unsaid, the a of buena Pidal's (house: 'he who in a good hour girded on his sword'); cinxo without the cedilla, as printed. serién, conditional, 'would be'. tacha, 'blemish, stain', dishonour. Nos = non + se (not 'we'): repentir(se), 'to repent, go back on'. casadas las ha, 'he has them married', the participle agreeing with las, as at v. 2606. amas, 'both'. The tirada ends on the first foreboding of Corpes.
